_metadata.description: Campaign profile for MITRE ATT&CK C0062 (AI-orchestrated Campaign / GTG-1002), for intelligence-led emulation and detection engineering. Built from public MITRE ATT&CK data (https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0062/).
_metadata.attribution_caution: Emulates documented TTPs for defensive testing; not an attribution claim about any specific incident.

campaign.name: AI-orchestrated Campaign
campaign.targets: ~30 entities across technology, financial, chemical, and government sectors
campaign.summary: Human operators used AI agents and Model Context Protocol tooling to automate reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, lateral movement, credential harvesting, data analysis, and exfiltration with minimal human involvement — crafted prompts/personas were used to bypass AI guardrails.
campaign.why_it_matters_defensively: First-class example of AI-orchestrated intrusion: the standard kill chain executed at machine speed and scale. The individual TTPs are largely conventional and detectable; what changes is TEMPO and VOLUME. Defensive implication: shrink detection/response windows and lean on velocity/volume anomalies, because a human-paced playbook assumption no longer holds.

techniques.name: Obtain Capabilities: Artificial Intelligence
techniques.campaign_use: Obtained access to AI agent tooling to drive the intrusion
techniques.defensive_note: Not visible to the target; the takeaway is to assume commodity AI lowers the barrier to high-tempo intrusions

techniques.name: Obtain Capabilities: Tool
techniques.campaign_use: Obtained open-source pentest tools (scanners, crackers)
techniques.defensive_note: Standard commodity tooling — detect at use, not acquisition

techniques.name: Develop Capabilities: Exploits
techniques.campaign_use: Researched SSRF techniques and built custom exploit chains

techniques.name: Generate Content
techniques.campaign_use: Auto-generated attack documentation across phases

techniques.name: Compromise Infrastructure: Server
techniques.campaign_use: Operated dedicated servers for command execution and state

techniques.name: Active Scanning: Scanning IP Blocks
techniques.campaign_use: Scanned target IP ranges
techniques.detection_ref: recon/attack-surface.json R-SCAN-ACTIVE — perimeter IDS/firewall rate anomalies

techniques.name: Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning
techniques.campaign_use: Scanned to identify vulnerabilities and enumerate services
techniques.detection_ref: recon R-SCAN-ACTIVE — high-rate probing; a blue-team drill target

techniques.name: Gather Victim Host Information: Software
techniques.campaign_use: Catalogued services/data on discovered endpoints

techniques.name: Gather Victim Host Information: Client Configurations
techniques.campaign_use: Gathered details of high-value systems (DBs, orchestration platforms)

techniques.name: Gather Victim Network Information: Network Topology
techniques.campaign_use: Mapped complete network topology

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.campaign_use: Deployed a custom payload against an identified SSRF vulnerability
techniques.detection_ref: hunt-queries H-14 (web server process spawns a shell), H-15 (web-shell drop); WAF/SSRF egress monitoring

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.campaign_use: Used harvested credentials against internal APIs, DBs, registries
techniques.detection_ref: correlation C-01 (risky sign-in -> lateral movement); impossible-travel H-05

techniques.name: Valid Accounts: Local Accounts
techniques.campaign_use: Tested harvested credentials against discovered devices
techniques.detection_ref: auth anomaly: same local account authenticating across many hosts in a short window

techniques.name: Create Account: Local Account
techniques.campaign_use: Created local backdoor accounts to maintain access
techniques.detection_ref: Windows Event ID 4720 (user account created); alert on new local accounts on servers

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
techniques.campaign_use: Extracted authentication certificates from config files
techniques.detection_ref: file-access to known secret/cert paths by unusual process; this repo's own secret-scan pattern set

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.campaign_use: Queried DB user tables to enumerate high-privilege accounts
techniques.detection_ref: DB audit: unusual SELECT against user/privilege tables

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.campaign_use: Enumerated internal services via browser automation over MCP
techniques.detection_ref: east-west connection fan-out from a single host (see velocity note)

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.campaign_use: Identified sensitive data for extraction

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.campaign_use: Queried DBs for proprietary info and system configs

techniques.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
techniques.campaign_use: Gathered system network configurations

techniques.name: System Network Connections Discovery
techniques.campaign_use: Mapped internal architecture and access relationships

techniques.name: Automated Collection
techniques.campaign_use: Automatically collected/processed large data volumes without human direction
techniques.detection_ref: correlation A-02 (file-access spike above the account's own baseline) — the KEY AI-tempo signal

techniques.name: Data from Information Repositories: Databases
techniques.campaign_use: Queried internal DBs to extract proprietary/operational data
techniques.detection_ref: DB audit: bulk/rapid extraction volume anomaly

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.campaign_use: Gathered credentials, configs, sensitive data locally

techniques.name: Data Staged: Local Data Staging
techniques.campaign_use: Staged extracted data in structured markdown files before exfil
techniques.detection_ref: creation of large aggregated files prior to egress

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
techniques.campaign_use: Exfiltrated data summaries over a web service
techniques.detection_ref: hunt-queries H-13 (cloud exfil); egress volume/destination anomaly

highest_value_detections: T1119 Automated Collection + A-02 baseline spike — the clearest AI-tempo tell (machine-speed bulk collection)
T1190 SSRF exploit -> H-14/H-15 web-process-spawns-shell / web-shell drop
T1136.001 local backdoor account -> Event ID 4720 on servers
T1078 valid accounts -> C-01 risky-signin-to-lateral-movement correlation
T1567 exfil over web service -> H-13 egress anomaly
ai_orchestration_defensive_takeaways: Tempo collapses: recon-to-exfil runs at machine speed, so alert-to-response windows must shrink — automate containment where possible
Volume anomalies matter more than any single signal: baseline per-entity rates (A-02) catch machine-speed collection that human-paced thresholds miss
East-west fan-out from one host is a strong tell when discovery is automated (T1046/T1049 in minutes, not days)
The TTPs are conventional and detectable — AI changes speed/scale, not the fundamentals. Existing detections still work; tighten their latency.
